newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Aug 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Aug 15.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
PEOPLE'S DAILY
- Large companies and enterprise groups along east coast playing a key role in national economy.
- Premier Li Peng will visit Malaysia and Singapore from August 21 to 26.
- Central bank governeor Dai Xianglong says China well keep to its moderately tight monetary policy.
- Dai Xianglong says China will loan Thailand $1.0 billion as part of an international bailout package.
XINHUA DAILY TELEGRAPH
- The Chinese Communist Party says it has persistently fought corruption since its 14th National Congress in 1992.
-- News analysis says that China and United States are seeking common strategic interests and this will ensure success of Chinese President Jiang Zemin's state visit to United States in October
-- Dalian has revitalised some of its state-owned enterprises through bankruptcy, merger and using overseas investment funds.
LEGAL DAILY
- China uncovers more than one million smuggled compact discs from January to August of this year.
CHINA BUSINESS DAILY
- Disposable income of Shanghai residents reaches 667 yuan in July, exceeding the 661 yuan of disposable income in Guangdong.
FINANCIAL NEWS
- China's State Council orders stock markets to come under central control of China Securities Regulatory Commission.
- China to crack down on illegal pyramid schemes in August and September.
CHINA SECURITIES
- Chief accountant of the China Securities Regulatory Commission Zhang Weiguo says state firms must adapt to international laws and regulations.
- Vice Minister of the State Commission for Restructuring Economy Hong Hu says shareholding reform helps state firms adapt to the market.
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY DAILY
- Minister of Power Industry Shi Dazhen says China would build 81 power plants from 2000 to 2010, and electricty generation would reach 1,760 kilowatt hours per capita in 2010.
INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS DAILY
- Construction finished on China's first joint venture railway with Hong Kong, the Jinhua to Wenzhou railroad.
- Hainan Coconut group invests $50 million to set up a fruit cannery in the Philippines.
- Hai'er group begins construction of largest washing-machine plant in Asia.
CHINA DAILY
- A new national civil-service system has been implemented throughout China.
